blogs.title: Are Employers Really Prohibited from Charging Penalties? Minnesota’s Wage Law and the Limits on Employee-Requested Penalties
blogs.description: This post dissects the court’s ruling on the MPWA and MFLSA penalties, explaining why only the Commissioner can impose daily‑average‑wage penalties, the statutory framing that precludes employee‑sued penalties, and the broader implications for wage‑law litigation in Minnesota. It also looks at how this decision affects the strategy of plaintiffs in future overtime cases.

blogs.title: Mootness and the Four‑Year‑Old Overtime Policy: How the Eighth Circuit Tackled MFLSA Penalties
blogs.description: Here we focus on the court’s refusal to grant summary judgment on Cohen’s MFLSA penalty claim, examining the standing and mootness analysis under Friends of the Earth and the practical impact of policy changes. The commentary explores the nuanced difference between cessation of wrongdoing, potential future violations, and the court’s jurisdictional concerns.

blogs.title: Class Action Politics in Wage‑Theft Cases: The Strategy Behind Pronounced Settlement Lumps and Litigant Inference
blogs.description: This piece explores the strategic choreography behind Cohen’s sizable settlement and the stipulation of “all wages and liquidated damages paid.” It evaluates how vendors and plaintiffs negotiate settlement outcomes versus the court’s obligation to scrutinize the underlying facts and the emerging trend of treatment of collective wage‑theft claims in the 8th Circuit.
